source_units: CopySkipper is a macOS one-way folder sync app that makes rsync-style copying easier to review, repeat, and trust.
It is intentionally simple: drag Source and Target folders, preview the job, then sync with a friendly UI.
Drop Source and Target folders, then press Sync now.
sync from Source → Target. It does not merge changes both ways.
: runs sync automatically at the selected interval (for example every 5 minutes).
(delete extra items in the target folder): removes files that exist only in the Target. This is equivalent to using rsync with
: shows a macOS notification after sync completes.
: opens the log panel so you can see what happened during the last run.
How do I cancel a running sync?
Deletions and metadata updates can move the progress bar slowly at first. The final completion state is accurate.
Auto-run triggers after a sync completes and the selected interval elapses.
Is this safe? Will it delete my files?
By default, CopySkipper copies Source → Target. Deletions happen only if you enable
). When in doubt, test with a small folder first.
Send bug reports or feature requests to
. Please include: app version, macOS version, and steps to reproduce.
